title: Subject-First Full Agreement
lede: When a human subject is named first, the following verb mirrors its person, gender and number. Learn the complete pattern—and the non-human plural exception.

items.feedback: Masculine singular subject → masculine singular verb.
Feminine singular subject → feminine singular verb.
Human masculine dual subject first → dual verb.
Human feminine plural subject first → feminine plural verb.
A non-human plural takes feminine singular agreement.

items.prompt: What controls the verb after a subject-first human noun?
items.feedback: Full agreement means all three features are visible.
Masculine dual subject first → شَرَحَا.
Feminine dual subject first → شَرَحَتَا.
Human masculine plural subject first → plural verb.
Human feminine plural subject first → feminine plural verb.
Feminine dual subject first → تـ + ـانِ.
Human masculine/mixed plural → يدرسون.
Third-person feminine plural present uses يـ + ـنَ.
Human plural subject first requires plural verb.
Human feminine plural → feminine plural verb.
Non-human plural → feminine singular.
Human masculine/mixed plural → plural agreement.
Non-human plural → feminine singular present.
Feminine singular full agreement.
Masculine dual subject first.
Feminine dual subject first.
Human masculine/mixed plural full agreement.
Human feminine plural full agreement.
Feminine dual present begins with تـ.
Third-person feminine plural future retains يـ + ـنَ.
Non-human plural → feminine singular present.
Mixed human plural → masculine plural agreement.

All plural subjects always take plural verbs.

games.e: Third-person feminine plural uses يـ + ـنَ.
Mixed human plural uses masculine plural agreement.

blocks: ## Why this matters لِمَاذَا نُطَابِقُ الْفِعْلَ؟
A subject-first sentence places a person or group at the centre. The verb must then give accurate information about that subject.
### Core
Match singular masculine and feminine subjects.
### Develop
Control dual and human plural agreement in three time frames.
### Stretch
Handle non-human plurals and coordinated subjects accurately.
[callout] Communication target: describe what different people and groups did, do and will do without confusing singular and plural endings.
## Diagnostic start
Use the feedback to locate the agreement family that needs review.
## The core subject-first rule
With an explicit human subject before the verb, the verb normally shows full agreement.
[callout] Memory line: الْفَاعِلُ أَوَّلًا ← مُطَابَقَةٌ كَامِلَةٌ — subject first means full agreement.

TABLE: Subject feature | Question | Verb signal // Person | Who: I, you, he, she, we, they? | prefix and/or suffix // Gender | Masculine or feminine? | e.g. كَتَبَ / كَتَبَتْ // Number | Singular, dual or plural? | e.g. كَتَبَ / كَتَبَا / كَتَبُوا
[ar] أَنَا كَتَبْتُ الرِّسَالَةَ.
[ar] الطَّالِبَتَانِ كَتَبَتَا الرِّسَالَةَ.
[ar] الطَّالِبَاتُ كَتَبْنَ الرِّسَالَةَ.
[ar] الطُّلَّابُ كَتَبُوا الرِّسَالَةَ.
## Past-tense full agreement
Past-tense endings carry the subject information after the preposed noun.

TABLE: Subject first | Agreeing verb | Complete sentence // الطَّالِبُ | كَتَبَ | الطَّالِبُ كَتَبَ الْوَاجِبَ. // الطَّالِبَةُ | كَتَبَتْ | الطَّالِبَةُ كَتَبَتِ الْوَاجِبَ. // الطَّالِبَانِ | كَتَبَا | الطَّالِبَانِ كَتَبَا الْوَاجِبَ. // الطَّالِبَتَانِ | كَتَبَتَا | الطَّالِبَتَانِ كَتَبَتَا الْوَاجِبَ. // الطُّلَّابُ | كَتَبُوا | الطُّلَّابُ كَتَبُوا الْوَاجِبَ. // الطَّالِبَاتُ | كَتَبْنَ | الطَّالِبَاتُ كَتَبْنَ الْوَاجِبَ.
[callout] Connected reading: In الطَّالِبَةُ كَتَبَتِ الْوَاجِبَ , a helping kasra may be heard on the feminine تْ before the article. The underlying past ending remains feminine singular.
## Present-tense full agreement
The present uses person prefixes plus dual/plural suffixes.

TABLE: Subject first | Agreeing present | Meaning // الطَّالِبُ | يَكْتُبُ | he writes // الطَّالِبَةُ | تَكْتُبُ | she writes // الطَّالِبَانِ | يَكْتُبَانِ | the two male/mixed students write // الطَّالِبَتَانِ | تَكْتُبَانِ | the two female students write // الطُّلَّابُ | يَكْتُبُونَ | the male/mixed students write // الطَّالِبَاتُ | يَكْتُبْنَ | the female students write
[callout] Two jobs for تـ: تَكْتُبُ may mean “she writes” or “you (m.) write”. The explicit subject and context resolve the meaning.
## Future agreement follows the present form
The future markers attach to or precede an already agreeing present-tense verb.
[ar] الطَّالِبُ سَيَكْتُبُ غَدًا.
[ar] الطَّالِبَةُ سَتَكْتُبُ غَدًا.
[ar] الطَّالِبَانِ سَيَكْتُبَانِ غَدًا.
[ar] الطَّالِبَتَانِ سَتَكْتُبَانِ غَدًا.
[ar] الطُّلَّابُ سَيَكْتُبُونَ غَدًا.
[ar] الطَّالِبَاتُ سَيَكْتُبْنَ غَدًا.
[callout] With سَوْفَ: keep the same agreeing present form: الطَّالِبَاتُ سَوْفَ يَكْتُبْنَ .
## The essential exception: non-human plurals
A non-human plural is normally treated as feminine singular in agreement, even when it appears before the verb.

TABLE: Non-human plural subject | Correct verb | Complete model // الْحَافِلَاتُ | وَصَلَتْ | الْحَافِلَاتُ وَصَلَتْ مُبَكِّرًا. // الْكُتُبُ | وَصَلَتْ | الْكُتُبُ وَصَلَتْ أَمْسِ. // الْمَدَارِسُ | تَفْتَحُ | الْمَدَارِسُ تَفْتَحُ أَبْوَابَهَا صَبَاحًا. // السَّيَّارَاتُ | سَتَتَوَقَّفُ | السَّيَّارَاتُ سَتَتَوَقَّفُ هُنَا.
[callout/warning] Do not overapply full plural agreement: الْحَافِلَاتُ وَصَلْنَ treats buses as a human feminine group. The standard target is الْحَافِلَاتُ وَصَلَتْ .
## Stretch: coordinated human subjects
When two named human subjects are placed first, treat the complete group as plural.
[ar] عَلِيٌّ وَأَحْمَدُ ذَهَبَا إِلَى السُّوقِ.
[ar] مَرْيَمُ وَلَيْلَى ذَهَبَتَا إِلَى السُّوقِ.
[ar] الطُّلَّابُ وَالطَّالِبَاتُ شَارَكُوا فِي الْمَشْرُوعِ.
[ar] أَنَا وَأُخْتِي ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى الْمَكْتَبَةِ.
[callout] Exam-safe strategy: For a complex coordinated subject, place the full subject first and use clear full agreement. This avoids the subtler agreement choices of verb-first coordination.
## Misconception and proofreading clinic
Correct only the agreement signal that conflicts with the subject.

TABLE: Incorrect | Correct | Repair // الطُّلَّابُ كَتَبَ الْوَاجِبَ. | الطُّلَّابُ كَتَبُوا الْوَاجِبَ. | Human plural subject first → plural verb. // الطَّالِبَاتُ يَكْتُبُونَ. | الطَّالِبَاتُ يَكْتُبْنَ. | Human feminine plural needs ـنَ. // الطَّالِبَتَانِ سَيَكْتُبَانِ. | الطَّالِبَتَانِ سَتَكْتُبَانِ. | Feminine dual present/future begins with تـ. // الْكُتُبُ وَصَلْنَ. | الْكُتُبُ وَصَلَتْ. | Non-human plural → feminine singular agreement.
## Grammar game
Match each subject-first noun phrase with the only verb form that agrees fully.
## Skills workshop التَّطْبِيقُ الْعَمَلِيُّ
Transform profiles and reports from singular to dual and plural without losing agreement.
[ar] الطَّالِبُ قَدَّمَ عَرْضًا، وَالطَّالِبَانِ أَجَابَا عَنِ السُّؤَالَيْنِ.
[ar] الطَّالِبَاتُ سَيَكْتُبْنَ تَقْرِيرًا، أَمَّا الْحَوَاسِيبُ فَسَتَعْمَلُ بِسُرْعَةٍ.
### Write a group progress report
Write 80–100 Arabic words describing what one person, two people and several groups did, do and will do in a school project.
[callout] Model: الطَّالِبَةُ جَمَعَتِ الْمَعْلُومَاتِ، وَالطَّالِبَانِ كَتَبَا التَّقْرِيرَ. الطَّالِبَاتُ يُرَاجِعْنَ النَّصَّ الآنَ، وَالصُّوَرُ سَتَظْهَرُ فِي الْعَرْضِ.

[callout] Success checklist: Use one masculine singular, one feminine singular, one dual, one human masculine/mixed plural, one human feminine plural and two non-human plural subjects. Keep every subject before its verb.
[callout] Paper route: Draw three columns—past, present and future. Place each subject in a row and write the fully agreeing verb beside it.
## Final mastery check
Check full agreement and the non-human plural exception.
### What you can now do
- Apply full agreement after a singular, dual or human plural subject.
- Control past, present and future subject-first forms.
- Use feminine plural verbs accurately with human feminine groups.
- Apply feminine singular agreement to non-human plural subjects.
Spaced revisit: Return in two or three days and complete the final check again without looking at the tables.
